card.title: BUFFS
card.text: Gets +1+1 when it is targeted by an order or deployment effect.
card.flavorText: The Buffs, officially known as the Royal East Kent Regiment, was an infantry regiment of the British Army with a long history dating back to 1572. During WWII, the Buffs played an active role across multiple theatres of combat as the regiment's battalions were mobilized and deployed extensively. The 1st Battalion fought in the North African Campaign, where they engaged Axis forces during crucial battles, including Operation Crusader and the fierce fighting around Tobruk and El Alamein. Following their success in North Africa, the battalion participated in the Italian campaign, where it faced fierce resistance at Monte Cassino and contributed significantly to the Allied advance. Meanwhile, the 2nd Battalion experienced intense combat in the Far East, defending Malaya against the Japanese invasion in 1941. They suffered heavy losses, and many troops endured years of harsh captivity as prisoners of war after the fall of Singapore. The 4th Battalion served in France in 1940, and after being evacuated at Dunkirk it was transferred to Malta where it defended against the Axis siege of the island. After the end of the siege, the battalion fought in the Battle of Leros, Greece, in 1943 where it surrendered after intense fighting. The 5th Battalion was also heavily involved in the Battle of France in 1940, where it fought bravely during the defense of key positions but suffered substantial casualties before being evacuated from Dunkirk. Later the 5th was reformed and saw further action in North Africa and Italy. Territorial battalions of the Buffs served with distinction as well, primarily within the British Isles and later in Northwest Europe after D-Day.
